description: Single-panel, black-and-white equilibrium phase diagram: the Fe-rich portion of the binary Fe-Al system, redrawn after Kubaschewski, with Al content on the abscissa (wt%, 0-40, ticks every 5) and Temperature on the ordinate (°C, 200-1600, ticks every 200). Labelled fields: liquid L across the top; a narrow γ field at the pure-Fe end bounded by 1392 °C at its top and 911 °C at its bottom; α (A2) filling most of the upper-left; the large central FeAl (B2) field; Fe3Al (DO3) at low temperature (roughly 13-22 wt% Al); two-phase α+FeAl, α+Fe3Al, L+α, FeAl+ε at top right and FeAl+FeAl2 at the far right. Printed temperatures include 1536 °C (Fe melting), 1310 °C, 1215 °C, 1092 °C and 552 °C. A dashed curve labelled "Magnetic transformation" descends from the α region toward ~550 °C, and dotted curves K1 and K2 delimit the low-temperature zone (about 8-24 wt% Al) where the so-called K-state exists; an arrow with the label 552 °C marks the α+FeAl / Fe3Al (DO3) boundary near 13 wt% Al. No boundary composition for the A2→B2 ordering is printed. The figure defines the phase fields through which ordered ferrite in Fe-Al(-Mn-C) steels passes.

observations.observation: The diagram is a single unscaled panel plotting Temperature (°C) vertically from 200 to 1600 (ticks every 200) against Al (wt%) horizontally from 0 to 40 (ticks every 5).
Labelled single-phase fields visible are L, γ, α (A2), FeAl (B2), Fe3Al (DO3) and FeAl+FeAl2; labelled two-phase fields are L+α, α+FeAl, α+Fe3Al and FeAl+ε.
Printed temperatures on the diagram are 1536 °C (pure-Fe melting at 0 wt% Al), 1392 °C and 911 °C bracketing the γ field, 1310 °C, 1215 °C, 1092 °C in the region between L+α and FeAl+ε, and 552 °C.
A dashed curve labelled "Magnetic transformation" descends from the α (A2) field toward roughly 550 °C across about 0-13 wt% Al.
Two dotted curves labelled K1 and K2 delimit a low-temperature band extending from about 8 to 24 wt% Al, the region the caption calls the K-state.
An arrow labelled 552 °C points to the boundary between the α+FeAl and Fe3Al (DO3) fields at about 13 wt% Al.
The caption states that phase boundaries for α, α (A2), FeAl (B2) and Fe3Al (DO3) are shown together with the area in which the so-called K-state exists.
The caption states the diagram is the Fe-rich part of the Fe-Al system according to Kubaschewski [88].
The citing text states that ferritic Fe-Al steels are principally based on the binary Fe-Al phase diagram.

The citing text states that predictions place the disorder-order transition of BCC_A2 (α) to BCC_B2 at an Al content higher than 2%, lower than the value obtained from experiments, referencing this figure.
The citing text states that the disorder-order transition temperature increases with increasing Al and Mn contents but decreases with increasing C content.
No numeric composition value for the α (A2) / FeAl (B2) ordering boundary is printed anywhere on the phase diagram; only the field labels are present.
The FeAl (B2) field spans the widest composition range of any ordered field shown, extending from roughly 22 to about 33 wt% Al between the α+FeAl and FeAl+FeAl2 regions.

unreadable_items: composition limits of the individual phase boundaries (no numeric values are printed for the α (A2)/FeAl (B2) or α+FeAl/Fe3Al (DO3) boundaries; only a few temperature labels are given)
the extreme right edge of the diagram near 40 wt% Al is cut off so the FeAl2 field boundary is only partially shown
